## Trial `mount-option-hardening-rhel7__FvsudrY`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor correctly hardened /tmp (via a systemd tmp.mount drop-in) and /dev/shm (via /etc/fstab) with noexec,nosuid,nodev, functionally verified each control (exec blocked, nodev-open blocked, nosuid flag present) before and after a real reboot confirmed by a boot_id change matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and left no residue behind. All material outcomes are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.950 | 0.930 | 13/3 (+1 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **tmp-hardening — Satisfied:** /tmp mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev on node1
  - **Why:** tmp.mount was given a systemd drop-in setting Options=mode=1777,strictatime,noexec,nosuid,nodev, enabled, and started. mount output (cmd-4b600e0e8d7b4eea) shows 'tmpfs on /tmp type tmpfs (rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,seclabel)'. Functional exec test on /tmp returned exit 126 both pre- and post-reboot (cmd-ccbbb76ead864f15, cmd-b4e14b622ab740f1).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ffa5f55e1dee42ca`, `cmd-c1feb97277b04829`, `cmd-892d2d771f0e42bf`, `cmd-4b600e0e8d7b4eea`, `cmd-ccbbb76ead864f15`, `cmd-b4e14b622ab740f1`
- **shm-hardening — Satisfied:** /dev/shm mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev on node1
  - **Why:** A /dev/shm entry with options defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec was added to /etc/fstab and the mount was remounted live; mount output (cmd-06252e56b6ea41c9) confirms 'rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec'. Exec test returned exit 126 both pre- and post-reboot (cmd-ccbbb76ead864f15, cmd-b4e14b622ab740f1), and the fstab entry persisted post-reboot (cmd-c349723e524c4c53).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-82dd3b131ac04cdf`, `cmd-06252e56b6ea41c9`, `cmd-ccbbb76ead864f15`, `cmd-b4e14b622ab740f1`, `cmd-c349723e524c4c53`
- **setuid-ignored — Satisfied:** Setuid bits are ignored on /tmp and /dev/shm
  - **Why:** Both mounts show the nosuid flag in mount output, the kernel-level mechanism that causes setuid/setgid bits on executables to be ignored. A setuid-copied binary could not be exercised because noexec already blocks execution on the same filesystems, so enforcement rests on the nosuid mount flag itself rather than a live privilege-escalation demonstration; this is a reasonable and standard verification given the overlapping controls.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4b600e0e8d7b4eea`, `cmd-06252e56b6ea41c9`, `cmd-ccbbb76ead864f15`
- **device-nodes-ignored — Satisfied:** Device nodes are ignored (nodev) on /tmp and /dev/shm
  - **Why:** A character device node (mknod c 1 3) was created on both mounts, and attempting to open/read it via cat failed with exit 1 on both, directly demonstrating nodev enforcement beyond just the mount flag (cmd-d3982d2514e3430d).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d3982d2514e3430d`
- **persist-reboot — Satisfied:** Hardening settings survive a reboot
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (f0f8b8e0...) and healthy hardened-mount baseline were captured (cmd-c349723e524c4c53), a reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-0faea2084d2842ad), the node was observed briefly unreachable (cmd-21a1a8955473419d), and a new boot_id (50e13c78...) with ~7.7s uptime was confirmed (cmd-53aee9eab6884aa3). Post-reboot re-verification (cmd-b4e14b622ab740f1) shows both /tmp and /dev/shm retaining nosuid,nodev,noexec and the noexec enforcement test again returning exit 126 on both. The boot-identity transition also matches the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor snapshots (f0f8b8e0 -> 50e13c78).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c349723e524c4c53`, `cmd-0faea2084d2842ad`, `cmd-21a1a8955473419d`, `cmd-53aee9eab6884aa3`, `cmd-b4e14b622ab740f1`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.950**. All executor mutations were purposeful and bounded. Test artifacts created during verification (t.sh, setuidtest, nulltest in /tmp and /dev/shm) were cleaned up within the same or an immediately following command (cmd-ccbbb76ead864f15 attempted removal, cmd-e5c65652eaae49b7 completed removal of the leftover device node with sudo rm -f, confirmed gone). The final nodev-proof mknod test (cmd-d3982d2514e3430d) removed its own device node in the same command. The disappearance of pre-existing /tmp/builder.log and systemd-private directories in the after_executor snapshot is an expected side effect of remounting /tmp as a fresh tmpfs via tmp.mount, not executor residue. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no unrestored state were observed.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-ccbbb76ead864f15`, `cmd-e5c65652eaae49b7`, `cmd-d3982d2514e3430d`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- Setuid enforcement was verified via the nosuid mount flag and inability to execute at all (due to noexec), rather than via a direct demonstration of a setuid binary retaining its ownership but losing its privilege when actually executed; this is standard but slightly less direct than the nodev proof.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.950); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.930; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
